intent.raw_query: Bali for solo traveler, $1500 budget, beaches and yoga, July 2026 from LA

experiences.name: Sunrise Yoga at Campuhan Ridge Walk
experiences.description: Join an outdoor sunrise yoga session along the scenic Campuhan Ridge Walk in Ubud, surrounded by lush green hills and rice paddies. Many local instructors offer small group classes here, blending breathwork and asana with Bali's natural beauty.

experiences.name: Seminyak Beach Sunset & Surf
experiences.description: Spend an afternoon at Seminyak Beach, one of Bali's most beautiful stretches of golden sand. Take a beginner surf lesson with a local instructor, then relax and watch the legendary Bali sunset. Surf lessons typically include board rental and a one-hour guided session.

experiences.name: Multi-Day Yoga Retreat at The Yoga Barn
experiences.description: Attend several drop-in yoga and meditation classes over your stay at The Yoga Barn, one of Bali's most renowned wellness centers. Classes range from Hatha and Vinyasa to Yin and sound healing, set in open-air jungle pavilions. Budget covers approximately 4–5 drop-in sessions.

experiences.name: Nusa Dua Crystal-Clear Beach Day
experiences.description: Escape to the calm, turquoise waters of Nusa Dua, Bali's most pristine beach area. Enjoy snorkeling, paddleboarding, or simply lounging on white sand. Equipment rentals are affordable and the water is ideal for swimming with excellent visibility.

experiences.name: Balinese Cooking Class & Temple Visit
experiences.description: Experience authentic Balinese culture with a morning cooking class where you visit a local market, learn to prepare traditional dishes like satay lilit and black rice pudding, followed by a guided visit to the nearby Tirta Empul water temple for a cultural blessing ceremony.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Bali
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Take a pre-booked budget airport shuttle or grab a Grab/Gojek ride to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled into your beachfront room.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack from a local warung (Indonesian street food stall) near the resort or order simple room service if available. Budget: ~IDR 30,000–50,000 (~$2–3 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Keep essentials in your carry-on for easy access upon arrival. Download Grab and Gojek apps before landing for cheap local transport. Exchange a small amount of cash at the airport for immediate needs.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After waking, take a relaxed stroll along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort to soak in your first Bali sunrise. Explore the immediate beach area, dip your toes in the warm Indian Ocean, and get oriented with the surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a nearby local market or minimart to stock up on snacks, water, and essentials. Spend the afternoon relaxing on the beach, swimming, or simply unwinding. Rent a sun lounger if available for a small fee (~IDR 20,000–30,000).
day_by_day.evening: Watch the famous Bali sunset from the beach. Explore the nearest beachside strip for dinner at a local warung. Try nasi goreng (fried rice) or mie goreng (fried noodles) — classic budget-friendly Balinese staples.

meals.breakfast: Warung breakfast near the resort — nasi goreng or bubur ayam (chicken porridge) with tea. Budget: ~IDR 25,000–40,000 (~$1.50–2.50 USD)
meals.lunch: Fresh fruit from a beach vendor or a simple meal at a local warungs — gado-gado (vegetable salad with peanut sauce). Budget: ~IDR 30,000–50,000
meals.dinner: Local warung dinner — nasi campur (mixed rice plate) with grilled fish or tempeh. Budget: ~IDR 40,000–60,000 (~$2.50–4 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is intentionally light to help you recover from jet lag. Stay hydrated in the warm 25°C weather. Sunscreen is a must — UV index in Bali is high even on cloudy days.

day_by_day.morning: Join a free or donation-based sunrise yoga session on the beach. Many beachfront areas in Bali have community yoga gatherings or affordable classes (~IDR 50,000–100,000). Practice facing the ocean for a truly magical experience. Bring a reusable water bottle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearest beach village on foot or by rented bicycle (~IDR 50,000/day). Visit local temples near the shoreline, observe daily Balinese Hindu offerings (canang sari), and browse small artisan shops for affordable souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a beachside café for a Bali sunset cocktail or fresh coconut. Many happy hour deals offer 2-for-1 drinks. Enjoy the laid-back Bali evening vibe with live acoustic music if available nearby.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl or banana pancakes at a budget café near the resort. Budget: ~IDR 35,000–55,000
meals.lunch: Warung lunch — sate lilit (Balinese minced fish satay) with rice. Budget: ~IDR 30,000–50,000
meals.dinner: Beachside warung — grilled corn, tempeh, and nasi putih (steamed rice). Budget: ~IDR 40,000–65,000

day_by_day.notes: Look for yoga studios or beach yoga groups on Facebook groups like 'Bali Expats' or notice boards at local cafés. Renting a bicycle is eco-friendly and a great way to explore at your own pace.

day_by_day.morning: Take a Grab or Gojek to visit a nearby iconic beach — such as Seminyak, Kuta, or Jimbaran depending on your resort's location. Walk the shoreline, people-watch, and enjoy the surf culture. Non-surfers can watch from the shore for free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby Hindu sea temple (such as Tanah Lot or Pura Uluwatu if within reasonable distance). Entry fees are typically IDR 30,000–60,000. Enjoy the dramatic coastal scenery and learn about Balinese spirituality.
day_by_day.evening: If visiting Uluwatu area, catch the famous Kecak Fire Dance performance at sunset (~IDR 150,000 — worth the splurge). Return to resort by Grab/Gojek.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the resort or a nearby café — toast, eggs, and Bali coffee (kopi Bali). Budget: ~IDR 30,000–50,000
meals.lunch: Beachside warung at the visited beach — fresh seafood plate or nasi goreng. Budget: ~IDR 40,000–70,000
meals.dinner: Jimbaran-style grilled seafood at a local (not tourist-priced) warung — grilled fish, squid, and rice. Budget: ~IDR 60,000–90,000

day_by_day.notes: The Kecak Dance at Uluwatu is a highlight of any Bali trip and is extremely budget-friendly for the experience it offers. Book transport in advance via Grab to avoid overpriced tourist taxis.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga at a local studio — look for drop-in classes at budget studios (~IDR 80,000–120,000 per class). Many studios offer multi-class passes for better value. Focus on a vinyasa or hatha flow to energize for the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the beach — try snorkeling if gear rental is available nearby (~IDR 50,000–80,000 for equipment). The warm clear waters around Bali are great for spotting colorful fish even for beginners.
day_by_day.evening: Explore a local night market (pasar malam) if one operates near your resort. Sample street food like martabak (stuffed pancake), pisang goreng (fried banana), and fresh juices.

meals.breakfast: Local warungs — bubur ayam or nasi goreng with a fried egg. Budget: ~IDR 25,000–40,000
meals.lunch: Post-yoga smoothie and avocado toast at a budget health café. Budget: ~IDR 45,000–65,000
meals.dinner: Night market street food spread — try 3–4 different dishes for variety. Budget: ~IDR 40,000–70,000

day_by_day.notes: Check local Facebook groups or Instagram for budget yoga studios with drop-in rates. Many studios offer free first classes as promotions. Snorkeling is best done in the morning when visibility is clearest.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ubud — Bali's cultural heart. Take a shared shuttle from your area (~IDR 50,000–75,000 one way). Start with a visit to the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary (entry ~IDR 80,000). Walk the forest trails and observe the playful long-tailed macaques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ubud's main street and traditional art market (Pasar Seni Ubud). Practice your bargaining skills for handmade crafts, sarongs, and souvenirs. Visit the Ubud Palace (Puri Saren) — free to enter the outer courtyard.
day_by_day.evening: Catch a traditional Legong or Barong dance performance in Ubud (~IDR 100,000–150,000). Return to resort via shared shuttle or Grab. Arrive back in the evening.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departing for Ubud. Budget: ~IDR 30,000–50,000
meals.lunch: Warung lunch in Ubud — nasi campur or lawar (traditional Balinese mixed dish). Budget: ~IDR 35,000–55,000
meals.dinner: Dinner in Ubud before heading back — try a local warungs near the market for authentic Balinese food. Budget: ~IDR 40,000–65,000

day_by_day.notes: Ubud is approximately 1–1.5 hours from coastal Bali depending on traffic. Start early to maximize your time. Wear a sarong at temples — many rent them for free at the entrance. Keep bags zipped around monkeys.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day. Start with a gentle morning meditation or yin yoga session on the beach at sunrise. Many resorts allow guests to practice yoga on the beach independently. Bring a mat or rent one from the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local area around Aegean Bliss Resort more deeply — find hidden beach spots, walk along the coast, or simply read a book under a palm tree. Visit a local coconut vendor for a fresh young coconut (~IDR 15,000–25,000).
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a budget-friendly traditional Balinese massage (~IDR 80,000–120,000 for 60 minutes) at a local spa near the resort. End the evening with a quiet dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort or nearby café — granola with fresh tropical fruit and Bali coffee. Budget: ~IDR 35,000–55,000
meals.lunch: Light warung lunch — gado-gado or cap cay (stir-fried vegetables). Budget: ~IDR 30,000–45,000
meals.dinner: Relaxed dinner at a local warung — soto ayam (chicken soup) with rice and iced tea. Budget: ~IDR 35,000–55,000

day_by_day.notes: Midway through the trip is a great time to rest and recharge. A traditional Balinese massage is one of the best budget splurges available — prices are a fraction of Western spa costs. Always confirm prices before the massage begins.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a nearby rice terrace — Tegallalang (near Ubud) or a smaller local terrace if closer to your resort. Entry fees are typically donation-based (~IDR 10,000–30,000). Walk the terraced paths and enjoy the lush green landscape unique to Bali.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at a local coffee plantation for a free tour and tasting of Kopi Luwak (civet coffee) and other Balinese coffees. Most plantations offer free tours with the expectation you may buy a small product — budget for ~IDR 30,000–50,000 if you choose to purchase.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and enjoy a casual evening on the beach. Watch the stars — Bali's coastal areas have beautiful night skies away from heavy light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Early warung breakfast — nasi goreng telur (fried rice with egg) and hot tea. Budget: ~IDR 25,000–40,000
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch — grab fresh fruit, bread, and local snacks from a minimart. Budget: ~IDR 25,000–40,000
meals.dinner: Beachside warung — mie goreng seafood with fresh lime juice. Budget: ~IDR 45,000–65,000

day_by_day.notes: The rice terraces are best visited in the morning before tour groups arrive. Wear comfortable walking shoes with grip as the paths can be muddy. Bring a light rain jacket — July can have occasional brief showers (30mm monthly average).

day_by_day.morning: Join a group yoga class at a well-reviewed local studio — try a different style today such as Kundalini or restorative yoga (~IDR 80,000–130,000). Many studios in Bali have world-class instructors at a fraction of Western prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a different beach for variety — explore tide pools, collect shells, or try stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) if available nearby (~IDR 100,000–150,000 per hour including basic instruction).
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local cooking class or food tour if budget allows (~IDR 150,000–250,000) to learn how to make Balinese dishes like satay, sambal, and lawar. Alternatively, cook a simple meal using fresh market ingredients if your accommodation has kitchen access.

meals.breakfast: Budget café — acai bowl or tropical fruit salad with coconut milk. Budget: ~IDR 40,000–60,000
meals.lunch: Post-yoga warung — tempeh manis (sweet tempeh) with rice and vegetables. Budget: ~IDR 30,000–50,000
meals.dinner: Cooking class dinner (included in class) OR local warung — bebek betutu (slow-cooked spiced duck) if budget allows as a splurge. Budget: ~IDR 60,000–100,000

day_by_day.notes: SUP is a fantastic low-impact beach activity great for yoga practitioners as it builds core strength and balance. Check weather conditions before paddleboarding — avoid going out if winds are strong.

day_by_day.morning: Take a sunrise trek or walk to a nearby viewpoint or hill for panoramic views of the coastline. Bring water and wear comfortable shoes. Alternatively, join a free beach clean-up organized by local eco-groups — a great way to give back.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local village near the resort on foot or by bicycle. Visit a traditional Balinese compound, observe daily life, and interact respectfully with locals. Stop at a roadside warung for refreshments.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost cultural event — check local notice boards or Bali tourism websites for community events, temple ceremonies open to respectful visitors, or free beach performances.

meals.breakfast: Pre-trek snack — banana and peanut butter toast from a local minimart. Budget: ~IDR 15,000–25,000
meals.lunch: Village warung lunch — simple nasi putih with side dishes (sayur urap, fried tofu, sambal). Budget: ~IDR 25,000–40,000
meals.dinner: Resort-area warung — ikan bakar (grilled fish) with steamed rice and fresh vegetables. Budget: ~IDR 50,000–75,000

day_by_day.notes: If attending a temple ceremony, dress modestly — wear a sarong and sash (often provided at temple entrances). Always follow local customs and ask permission before photographing ceremonies or people.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning beach day — swim, snorkel, or simply lounge. Rent a surfboard if interested (~IDR 50,000–80,000/hour) and take a beginner surf lesson (~IDR 150,000–200,000 including board) if you haven't tried surfing yet. Bali is one of the world's best places to learn.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local temple or cultural site in the afternoon when morning crowds have dispersed. Explore at a leisurely pace and reflect on your Bali journey so far.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset beach walk followed by dinner at a slightly nicer local restaurant as a mid-trip treat. Try a seafood platter or traditional rijsttafel (rice table) if available at an affordable local spot.

meals.breakfast: Hearty warung breakfast — nasi goreng special with chicken, egg, and prawn crackers. Budget: ~IDR 35,000–55,000
meals.lunch: Beach warung — fresh coconut, corn on the cob, and grilled skewers. Budget: ~IDR 30,000–50,000
meals.dinner: Slightly elevated local restaurant — seafood grilled platter with rice and sambal. Budget: ~IDR 80,000–120,000 (modest splurge)

day_by_day.notes: Surfing lessons are a must-do in Bali even for complete beginners. Instructors are patient and the waves in beginner zones are gentle. Always apply reef-safe sunscreen before entering the water.

day_by_day.morning: Final full yoga session — book a 90-minute class at your favorite studio discovered during the trip, or practice independently on the beach at sunrise for a meaningful closing ritual. Journal about your Bali experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at local markets — look for handmade batik fabrics, silver jewelry, wooden carvings, and Balinese spice sets. Bargain respectfully and remember to buy from local artisans rather than large tourist shops.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — choose a warung or local restaurant that became a favorite during your stay. Enjoy your last Bali sunset over the ocean and savor the final evening in paradise.

meals.breakfast: Final resort-area breakfast — tropical fruit platter, Bali coffee, and banana pancakes. Budget: ~IDR 40,000–60,000
meals.lunch: Light market lunch while shopping — martabak, pisang goreng, and fresh juice. Budget: ~IDR 30,000–50,000
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a favorite local warung — order your favorite Balinese dishes. Budget: ~IDR 60,000–100,000

day_by_day.notes: Pack souvenirs carefully — wooden items and certain foods may have import restrictions in your home country. Check customs regulations. Keep receipts for any purchases over a certain value.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Bali — wake up early for one last beach sunrise. Take photos, meditate, or simply sit and absorb the sounds of the ocean. Pack remaining belongings and do a thorough room check before checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Store luggage with the hotel if your flight is later in the day. Spend remaining time at the beach or a nearby café. Head to the airport with ample time — allow at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Bali — carry wonderful memories, a renewed yoga practice, and the spirit of the Island of the Gods with you.

meals.breakfast: Final warung breakfast — keep it simple and familiar. Nasi goreng and Bali coffee one last time. Budget: ~IDR 25,000–40,000
meals.lunch: Airport meal or a quick warung stop en route to the airport. Budget: ~IDR 40,000–80,000 (airport prices are higher)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Book your airport transfer in advance via Grab or a pre-arranged hotel taxi. Arrive at Ngurah Rai International Airport at least 3 hours before international departure. Keep travel documents, passport, and boarding pass easily accessible. Carry some Indonesian Rupiah for any last-minute airport purchases.

trip_options.title: Classic Bali Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and arrange a pre-booked airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront room.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Light snack or room service at the resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to avoid late-night taxi hassles. Confirm check-in details with the resort ahead of time. Keep the first night light — rest is the priority.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a gentle stroll along the beachfront to orient yourself with the surroundings and watch the morning waves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local beach area near the resort. Rent a sun lounger, take a dip in the warm Bali Sea, and browse nearby beachside shops for essentials. Grab a fresh coconut from a local vendor.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a nearby beachside warung (local eatery) for a relaxed first dinner in Bali. Watch the sunset from the beach before returning to the resort for an early night.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet — enjoy tropical fruits, nasi goreng, and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beachside café near the resort — try a fresh fish sandwich or gado-gado
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local warung near the beach — nasi campur or grilled fish with sambal (approx. IDR 60,000–100,000)

day_by_day.notes: Take it easy today — jet lag may still be a factor. Drink plenty of water and apply high-SPF sunscreen as the Bali sun is strong even in July.

day_by_day.morning: Join a sunrise yoga session on the beach or at the resort (many beachfront resorts in Bali offer complimentary or low-cost morning yoga). Practice breathwork and gentle asanas as the sun rises over the ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby surf school for a beginner or intermediate surf lesson. The warm July waters and consistent waves make this an ideal time. Most lessons run 2 hours and include board rental.
day_by_day.evening: Explore a local night market (pasar malam) in the nearest town for an authentic Balinese street food experience. Sample satay, martabak, and fresh fruit juices.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-yoga breakfast — banana, granola, and coconut water from a resort café
meals.lunch: Post-surf meal at a surf shack or warung near the beach — mie goreng or a fresh smoothie bowl
meals.dinner: Night market street food dinner — budget around IDR 50,000–80,000 for a full spread

day_by_day.notes: Book your surf lesson the evening before or early morning to secure a spot. Bring a rash guard to protect from sunburn during the surf session.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga class at a dedicated yoga studio nearby — look for a Vinyasa or Hatha flow class. Many studios in Bali offer drop-in classes for IDR 80,000–150,000. Follow with a healthy breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hire a local driver or rent a scooter to visit a nearby iconic Balinese temple such as Tanah Lot or Uluwatu (depending on your resort's location). Explore the temple grounds and learn about Balinese Hindu culture.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the famous Kecak Fire Dance performance at Uluwatu Temple at sunset — an unmissable cultural experience. Performances typically start around 18:00.

meals.breakfast: Post-yoga breakfast at a health café — avocado toast, acai bowl, or a green smoothie
meals.lunch: Lunch at a mid-range restaurant near the temple — try bebek betutu (slow-cooked duck) or lawar
meals.dinner: Seafood dinner at a cliffside restaurant near Uluwatu with ocean views (approx. IDR 150,000–250,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear or bring a sarong when visiting temples — many provide them at the entrance for a small fee. Book Kecak Dance tickets in advance during peak July season.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning beach walk to collect shells and watch local fishermen bring in their catch. Return for breakfast, then spend time journaling or meditating on your balcony or the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a day trip to a nearby waterfall or rice terrace (such as Tegalalang Rice Terraces in Ubud if within reach). Enjoy the lush green landscape and take photos. Walk the terraces and interact with local farmers.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Enjoy a traditional Balinese massage at a local spa — a one-hour massage typically costs IDR 100,000–200,000. Unwind with a quiet evening by the pool.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or a local café — try bubur ayam (chicken rice porridge) for an authentic start
meals.lunch: Warung lunch near the rice terraces — nasi goreng or mixed rice plate
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range restaurant with Balinese cuisine — try sate lilit and pelecing kangkung

day_by_day.notes: If visiting Tegalalang, go early (before 9:00) to avoid crowds and the midday heat. Entrance fees and swing/photo spot fees are separate — budget IDR 50,000–100,000 extra.

day_by_day.morning: Attend a two-hour yoga workshop focused on a specific theme — pranayama, meditation, or restorative yoga. Many Bali studios offer themed weekend workshops. This is a great way to deepen your practice.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the beach — snorkeling, paddleboarding, or simply relaxing. Rent equipment from a beachside vendor. The calm July waters are excellent for snorkeling around coral reefs.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a beachfront bar. Enjoy a Bali Sunset mocktail or local Bintang beer while watching the sky change colors. Dinner at a slightly upscale beachfront restaurant for a treat.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-workshop meal — fruit salad and herbal tea
meals.lunch: Post-beach lunch at a warung — fresh grilled fish, tempeh, and rice
meals.dinner: Beachfront restaurant dinner — grilled prawns, tuna steak, or a seafood platter (IDR 200,000–350,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check local yoga studio social media pages or noticeboards at the resort for upcoming workshops. Snorkeling gear rental is typically IDR 50,000–75,000 per hour.

day_by_day.morning: Full day trip to Ubud — the cultural heart of Bali. Start with a visit to the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary. Wander through the ancient temples and observe the resident macaques in their natural habitat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ubud's vibrant art market (Pasar Seni Ubud) for handmade crafts, textiles, and souvenirs. Visit the Ubud Palace (Puri Saren Agung) and stroll along Monkey Forest Road browsing galleries and boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Ubud before returning to the resort. Ubud has an excellent range of mid-range restaurants offering both Indonesian and international cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a popular Ubud warung or café — try Warung Ibu Oka for babi guling (suckling pig) or a vegetarian café on Jalan Dewi Sita
meals.dinner: Dinner in Ubud before heading back — try a restaurant with live traditional music for atmosphere (IDR 120,000–200,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Hire a private driver for the Ubud day trip for convenience — expect to pay IDR 400,000–600,000 for the full day. Hold onto your belongings at the Monkey Forest as monkeys can snatch items.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning. Sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, and spend time by the pool or beach reading. This mid-trip rest day is important for maintaining energy for the second half.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local cooking class in the afternoon — learn to make traditional Balinese dishes like satay, sambal, and black rice pudding. Classes typically last 3–4 hours and include a meal.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the meal you cooked! Most cooking classes end with eating what you've prepared. Return to the resort for a quiet evening — perhaps a moonlit beach walk.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast — take your time and try everything on the buffet
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort pool bar — a salad, sandwich, or fresh juice
meals.dinner: The dishes from your cooking class — a unique and memorable dining experience

day_by_day.notes: Book your cooking class at least 2 days in advance. Prices range from IDR 250,000–450,000 per person and usually include a market visit in the morning or afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning sunrise yoga on the beach — either a self-guided practice or a resort session. Follow with a swim in the ocean as the day heats up. This is a wonderful way to connect with nature.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a different beach section or nearby beach town. Visit local warungs, browse handicraft stalls, and interact with local vendors. Try a fresh young coconut and tropical fruits from roadside sellers.
day_by_day.evening: Book a traditional Balinese healing session (Melukat purification ritual or Balian healer visit) for a deeply cultural wellness experience. Alternatively, enjoy a couples or solo spa package at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Post-yoga smoothie bowl or fruit platter at a beachside health café
meals.lunch: Local warung lunch in the beach town — nasi campur with a selection of Balinese sides
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort restaurant for convenience — try the catch of the day or a Balinese set menu

day_by_day.notes: The Melukat ritual is typically held at a water temple and is a meaningful cultural experience. Arrange through your resort concierge or a trusted local guide. Dress modestly and bring a sarong.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a renowned beach on a different part of the Bali coastline — such as Nusa Dua, Seminyak, or Padang Padang Beach (depending on your resort location). Enjoy the different beach atmosphere and scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the beach area. Try stand-up paddleboarding or a banana boat ride for some fun. Browse the beach clubs and boutique shops in the area.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner at a beach club or cliffside restaurant in the area you've visited before returning to your resort.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Beach club or casual café lunch at your destination beach — a burger, salad, or Indonesian rice dish
meals.dinner: Sunset dinner with a view — grilled seafood or a shared platter (IDR 200,000–300,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Factor in travel time between beaches — Bali traffic can be unpredictable, especially in the afternoon. Allow at least 1–2 hours for travel each way depending on your location.

day_by_day.morning: Attend a morning meditation class or sound healing session — Bali has many wellness centers offering crystal bowl, gong bath, or guided meditation experiences. A deeply restorative experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local village near the resort — visit a traditional Balinese compound, observe daily offerings (canang sari), and learn about local customs and family temple structures from a guide.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local art gallery or cultural performance in the evening. Many towns in Bali host regular Legong or Barong dance performances. End the night at a cozy café with Balinese coffee.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-meditation breakfast — herbal tea and fruit
meals.lunch: Lunch at a warung in the village — home-cooked Balinese food, simple and authentic
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range restaurant with a cultural performance — enjoy the show while dining (IDR 100,000–200,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Sound healing sessions typically cost IDR 150,000–300,000. Village visits are best arranged through a local guide to ensure a respectful and meaningful experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning — wake up early for one last sunrise yoga or meditation on the sand. Swim, snorkel, or simply sit and absorb the beauty of the Bali coastline. Take photos and soak in the moment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Shopping afternoon — pick up last-minute souvenirs, Balinese textiles, essential oils, or handmade jewelry from local markets or boutique shops. Pack thoughtfully and start organizing your luggage.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at your favorite restaurant from the trip or try somewhere new that you've been meaning to visit. Celebrate the journey with a special meal and perhaps a cocktail.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — enjoy it fully as one of your last mornings
meals.lunch: Casual lunch while shopping — street food or a warung meal
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner — choose a restaurant that represents the best of your Bali experience. Splurge slightly on a beachfront or rooftop venue (IDR 250,000–400,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Bargaining is expected at local markets — start at 50% of the asking price and negotiate respectfully. Keep some cash in smaller denominations for market shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up at a comfortable time based on your departure flight. Enjoy a last breakfast at the resort. Take a final walk on the beach, breathe in the ocean air, and say goodbye to Bali.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Arrange airport transfer and head to Ngurah Rai International Airport. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Bali. Reflect on 13 incredible days of beaches, yoga, culture, and adventure as you fly home.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — enjoy tropical fruits, fresh juice, and your favorite dishes one last time
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or a quick bite near the resort before checkout
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure flight details and airport transfer the night before. Keep your travel documents, passport, and boarding pass easily accessible. Leave some Indonesian Rupiah for any last airport purchases or tips.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Bali Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled – in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 22:30. A private luxury transfer arranged by Aegean Bliss Resort whisks you to the hotel. Check in to your Beachfront suite, enjoy a welcome drink and a light late-night amenity platter prepared by the resort's kitchen team. Unwind on your private terrace to the sound of the Indian Ocean.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable – in transit
meals.lunch: Not applicable – in transit
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome amenity platter (charcuterie, tropical fruits, local sweets) served in-room by the resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Request the resort's 24-hour butler service to pre-chill your preferred beverages and draw a bath with Balinese floral oils before arrival. Keep Day 1 light – rest is the priority.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast on your beachfront terrace. After breakfast, take a gentle orientation stroll along the resort's private beach, getting acquainted with the coastline and the warm July surf. Meet your dedicated resort concierge to plan the days ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle into resort life with a two-hour introductory Hatha yoga session on the resort's open-air ocean-facing yoga pavilion led by a resident certified instructor. Follow with a refreshing dip in the infinity pool overlooking the sea, then indulge in a 90-minute Balinese massage at the resort's luxury spa.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at the resort's beachfront bar as the sun dips below the horizon. Enjoy a private candlelit dinner on the sand arranged by the resort's fine-dining team, featuring fresh Jimbaran-style grilled seafood and Indonesian specialties.

meals.breakfast: À la carte beachfront breakfast at the resort – fresh tropical juices, Balinese eggs Benedict, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort's cabana – grilled prawn skewers, coconut ceviche, and fresh smoothie bowls
meals.dinner: Private candlelit beach dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort – Jimbaran-style grilled lobster, whole fish, sate lilit, and coconut panna cotta for dessert

day_by_day.notes: July weather is ideal – warm with minimal rain. SPF 50+ and a wide-brim hat are recommended for afternoon beach time. Confirm the private beach dinner reservation with the butler by noon.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise beach yoga session (6:00–7:30 AM) on the private shoreline with the resort's senior yoga instructor, focusing on sun salutations and pranayama breathing. Afterward, enjoy a nourishing post-yoga breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private half-day snorkeling and sailing excursion departing from the resort's beach. Cruise along Bali's southwestern coastline on a luxury catamaran, stopping at two pristine snorkeling sites teeming with tropical fish and coral. Champagne and canapés served on deck.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and freshen up. Head out to a premium beachfront restaurant in the nearby Seminyak area for dinner – one of Bali's most celebrated dining strips. Return via private resort transfer.

meals.breakfast: Post-yoga wellness breakfast at the resort – acai bowls, avocado toast on sourdough, cold-pressed juices, and herbal teas
meals.lunch: Gourmet canapé and fresh fruit spread served on the catamaran deck with chilled Champagne
meals.dinner: Metis Restaurant, Seminyak – award-winning French-Mediterranean cuisine with Balinese influences in an elegant garden setting

day_by_day.notes: Book the catamaran excursion through the resort concierge at least 24 hours in advance. Bring reef-safe sunscreen and a light cover-up for the boat. Metis reservation recommended – concierge can arrange.

day_by_day.morning: Morning Vinyasa flow yoga class (7:00–8:30 AM) at the resort pavilion followed by a guided meditation session. After breakfast, take a private luxury vehicle to explore the artistic village of Seminyak and Petitenget – browse high-end boutiques, galleries, and local artisan studios.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the iconic Tanah Lot sea temple (approximately 45 minutes from Seminyak). Explore the dramatic coastal temple perched on a rocky outcrop with your private guide, learning about Balinese Hindu traditions and the temple's significance. The July dry season offers crystal-clear views.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a clifftop bar near Tanah Lot, then a private transfer back to the resort. Enjoy dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet with live cooking stations – Balinese nasi goreng, fresh pastries, tropical fruit platters, and barista coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium café in Seminyak – La Lucciola or similar beachfront venue – grilled fish, fresh salads, and tropical cocktails
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort signature restaurant – contemporary Indonesian tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly (sarong and sash required) for the Tanah Lot temple visit – these are typically provided at the entrance. Arrive at Tanah Lot by 4:30 PM for the best sunset vantage point.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Ubud begins with an early private transfer (approximately 1.5 hours). Start the morning with a visit to the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary and the ancient Ubud Palace. Stroll through the vibrant Ubud Art Market with your guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch in Ubud, visit the breathtaking Tegallalang Rice Terraces – a UNESCO-recognized cultural landscape. Enjoy a private guided walk through the emerald terraces. Then visit a premium local healer or Balinese wellness practitioner for a traditional blessing ceremony (melukat purification ritual).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a world-class Kecak fire dance performance at Uluwatu Temple at sunset (if returning via southern route) or a traditional Legong dance at the Ubud Palace. Private transfer back to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departure – yogurt parfait, fresh fruit, and espresso
meals.lunch: Lunch at Locavore or Hujan Locale, Ubud – celebrated farm-to-table Indonesian fine dining
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bridges Restaurant, Ubud – stunning jungle gorge views with contemporary European-Asian fusion cuisine, then transfer back to resort

day_by_day.notes: Ubud is approximately 1.5 hours from the resort. An early 7:30 AM departure is recommended to avoid midday heat. The Kecak dance at Uluwatu requires an additional 1-hour detour on the return journey – confirm with your driver.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and rejuvenation day. Begin with a 90-minute Yin yoga and sound healing session at the resort's wellness center. Follow with a private stretch and breathwork session with the resident yoga therapist.
day_by_day.afternoon: Full afternoon at the resort's luxury spa – book the 'Royal Bali Journey' package (approximately 3 hours) including a traditional Boreh herbal scrub, flower bath, Balinese massage, and facial treatment. Spend the remaining time floating in the resort's thalassotherapy pool.
day_by_day.evening: Private in-suite romantic dinner prepared by the resort's executive chef – a curated four-course Balinese feast served on your beachfront terrace under the stars with a dedicated butler in attendance.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast delivered to your terrace – freshly squeezed juices, Balinese banana pancakes, granola, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Healthy spa lunch at the resort wellness café – quinoa salads, cold-pressed juices, and raw energy bites
meals.dinner: Private four-course in-suite dinner on the beachfront terrace – chef's selection of Balinese and Indonesian delicacies with premium wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: This is a designated wellness and recovery day. Limit sun exposure and stay well-hydrated. Pre-book the Royal Bali Journey spa package through the butler at least 48 hours in advance as slots fill quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise surf lesson on the resort's private beach with a certified professional surf instructor (beginner to intermediate level). July's swells on Bali's southwest coast are ideal for learning. Follow with a refreshing outdoor shower and beachside coconut water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided visit to the Uluwatu area – explore the dramatic clifftop Uluwatu Temple with sweeping Indian Ocean views. Afterward, descend to the famous Padang Padang Beach and Bingin Beach for swimming and relaxation at an exclusive beach club.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Kecak fire dance performance at Uluwatu Temple (6:00 PM). Dinner at a premium clifftop restaurant in the Uluwatu area before private transfer back to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Post-surf beach breakfast at the resort – protein-rich eggs any style, smashed avocado, Balinese-spiced potatoes, and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Lunch at Single Fin or Sundays Beach Club, Uluwatu – fresh seafood, salads, and cocktails with panoramic ocean views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Savaya (formerly Omnia) Dayclub & Restaurant, Uluwatu – upscale Mediterranean cuisine on a spectacular clifftop terrace

day_by_day.notes: The surf lesson is best scheduled for 7:00–8:30 AM before the beach becomes crowded. Wear reef-safe sunscreen. Uluwatu Temple requires a sarong – provided at entrance. Book Savaya dinner well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Morning Ashtanga yoga practice (7:00–8:30 AM) at the resort pavilion. After breakfast, take a private boat transfer to Nusa Lembongan island (approximately 30–45 minutes from the mainland). Check in to a day-use arrangement or explore the island freely.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling at the famous Manta Point near Nusa Penida (seasonal – mantas are active July–October) via a private chartered speedboat. Swim alongside majestic oceanic manta rays in crystal-clear waters. Visit the iconic Kelingking Beach viewpoint on Nusa Penida for dramatic cliff-top photos.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the mainland via private speedboat. Freshen up at the resort and enjoy a relaxed dinner at a premium Seminyak beachfront restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure – smoothie bowls, eggs Benedict, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a beachside warung on Nusa Lembongan – grilled fish, coconut rice, and local sambal
meals.dinner: Dinner at Merah Putih Restaurant, Seminyak – stunning modern Indonesian cuisine in a dramatic high-ceilinged heritage building

day_by_day.notes: Manta Point sightings are highly likely in July but not guaranteed. Bring motion sickness tablets if prone to sea sickness – the Nusa Penida crossing can be choppy. Kelingking viewpoint requires a short steep hike – wear sturdy sandals.

day_by_day.morning: Gentle morning beach walk and meditation at sunrise. After breakfast, join a private Balinese cooking class at a premium culinary studio in the Seminyak or Canggu area – learn to prepare traditional dishes including sate, lawar, and black rice pudding.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the cooking class lunch, head to Canggu for an afternoon of exploration – visit the vibrant beach clubs, browse high-end surf and lifestyle boutiques, and take in the laid-back creative energy of Bali's trendiest coastal village. Optional: stand-up paddleboard session at Echo Beach.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at Finns Beach Club or similar premium Canggu venue. Return to the resort via private transfer for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – freshly baked croissants, tropical fruit platter, Balinese coffee, and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Feast on the dishes you prepared during the cooking class – an authentic Balinese spread enjoyed with fellow participants
meals.dinner: In-resort dining at the beachfront grill – premium wagyu beef, grilled lobster, and Balinese desserts with a curated cocktail menu

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class through the resort concierge. Canggu is approximately 20–30 minutes from Seminyak. July evenings can be lively in Canggu – the resort's private transfer ensures a comfortable return.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day private excursion to East Bali. Depart early by private luxury vehicle. Visit the majestic Besakih Temple – Bali's 'Mother Temple' – perched on the slopes of Mount Agung with a knowledgeable private guide explaining its spiritual significance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the serene Tirta Gangga Water Palace – a stunning royal garden complex with tiered fountains, koi-filled pools, and lush tropical grounds. Take a refreshing swim in the natural spring pools. Visit a nearby traditional Balinese village to observe daily life and local craftsmanship.
day_by_day.evening: Stop at Candidasa or Amed coastal area for a sunset dinner overlooking the Lombok Strait before the scenic private drive back to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium restaurant near Tirta Gangga – traditional Balinese rijsttafel (rice table) feast in a garden setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at a clifftop seafood restaurant in Candidasa or Amed – fresh grilled catch of the day with East Balinese spices and ocean views

day_by_day.notes: East Bali is approximately 2–2.5 hours from the resort. Depart by 7:00 AM to maximize time. Besakih Temple requires a local guide and appropriate dress. The drive through Bali's countryside offers spectacular volcanic scenery.

day_by_day.morning: Restorative morning – Yin yoga and pranayama session at the resort (7:00–8:30 AM). After breakfast, enjoy a private guided paddleboard yoga session on the calm morning waters just off the resort's private beach – a unique fusion of yoga and water sports.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury afternoon at leisure – spend time on the resort's private beach, read in a cabana, or take a refreshing swim. Optional: book a second spa treatment – a Javanese Lulur ritual (traditional royal body treatment) at the resort spa.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset catamaran cruise departing from the resort's beach – sip Champagne and enjoy canapés while watching the sun melt into the Indian Ocean. Return for a special resort chef's table dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Wellness breakfast at the resort – overnight oats, green smoothies, poached eggs, and herbal teas
meals.lunch: Poolside lunch at the resort – fresh tuna tataki, grilled vegetable platter, and tropical fruit sorbet
meals.dinner: Chef's table experience at Aegean Bliss Resort – exclusive six-course tasting menu prepared tableside by the executive chef with premium wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: The paddleboard yoga session requires calm sea conditions – the resort will confirm suitability on the morning. The chef's table experience accommodates a maximum of 6 guests and must be reserved 48 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final full-day adventure – private sunrise hike to the summit of Mount Batur (active volcano, 1,717m). Depart from the resort at 2:00 AM for the 2-hour drive to Kintamani. Begin the guided 2-hour ascent in darkness, arriving at the summit for a spectacular sunrise above the clouds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend Mount Batur and enjoy a well-earned brunch at a premium lakeside restaurant overlooking Lake Batur and the volcanic caldera. Return to the resort by early afternoon. Spend the remainder of the afternoon relaxing on the beach or at the spa – a final indulgent massage to soothe hiking muscles.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the resort's finest beachfront table – a celebratory à la carte dinner with the resort's sommelier selecting wines to accompany each course. Reflect on 13 days of extraordinary Balinese experiences.

meals.breakfast: Energy snack pack prepared by the resort for the pre-dawn hike – protein bars, bananas, and a thermos of Balinese coffee
meals.lunch: Post-hike brunch at Lakeview Restaurant, Kintamani – panoramic caldera views with a traditional Balinese buffet spread
meals.dinner: Farewell à la carte dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort beachfront – premium Wagyu tenderloin, whole steamed barramundi, and a Champagne dessert finale

day_by_day.notes: The Mount Batur hike departs at approximately 2:00 AM from the resort. A 2:30 AM arrival at the trailhead allows time for a 4:00 AM summit start. Bring warm layers (summit temperature can drop to 10°C), a headlamp, and sturdy hiking shoes. Book a certified guide through the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise yoga and meditation session on the beach (6:30–7:30 AM) – a mindful close to the Bali journey. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the resort, savoring the beachfront views one final time. Take a slow morning walk along the shoreline to collect memories and perhaps a few sea shells.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Depending on departure flight time, enjoy a final spa treatment or pool session before checkout. The resort's private luxury transfer takes you to Ngurah Rai International Airport in comfort and style.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Bali. Carry with you the warmth of Balinese hospitality, the scent of frangipani, and 13 days of extraordinary luxury experiences.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast – a special farewell spread prepared by the kitchen team, including Balinese favorites and international classics
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the resort or airport lounge – fresh salads, sandwiches, and tropical juices
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight meal (business/first class)

day_by_day.notes: Request a late checkout from the resort (typically until 2:00 PM with advance notice) to maximize your final morning. The resort's concierge can assist with luggage storage if needed. Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and immigration.
